the novel grouping algorithms outperform existing grouping algorithms, and that the proposed joint transmit and receive protocol is able to improve the attainable capacity of a MIMO-OFDM cellular network by up to a factor of 2.

the proposed grouping algorithms outperform the existing ones, and that the performance of the proposed grouping algorithms depends on the network topology, i.e. the number of relays and the number of users.

the proposed transmission protocol is able to achieve a higher capacity than the conventional one, and that the grouping algorithms proposed in this thesis are able to improve the capacity of this transmission protocol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new transmission protocol for a MIMO-OFDM cellular network based on the use of multiple relays and joint transmit and receive precoding.

the design and performance evaluation of a novel MIMO-OFDM transmission protocol, which is based on joint transmit-receive beamforming, and is suitable for a multi-user multi-relay MISO-OFDM cellular network.

a novel transmission protocol for a multi-user multi-relay multiple-input-multipleoutput orthogonal frequency-division-multipleaccess (MIMO- OFDMA) cellular network, based on joint transmit-receive beamforming.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in a multi-user, multiple-input-mutiple-output orthogonal frequency- division multiple-access cellular network based on transmit and receive beam- forming, the proposed grouping algorithms are able to achieve a better trade- off between the network's attainable capacity and complexity, compared to the conventional grouping algorithms, while the proposed transmission protocol is capable of attaining a better trade-off between the network's capacity and complexity, as compared to the conventional transmission protocol, which is based on the conventional grouping algorithms.
the proposed grouping algorithms outperform the conventional grouping algorithms in terms of the attainable capacity and the complexity.

the proposed grouping algorithms are very effective in improving the capacity of the MIMO-OFDM cellular networks, especially for the cases where the network is equipped with a large number of antennas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of the considered MIMO-OFDM system, we have proposed a novel joint beamforming transmission protocol that is able to exploit both the spatial multiplexing gains of the MIMO-OFDMS system and the diversity gains of the relay-assisted cellular network, in an efficient manner.
the joint transmit and receive scheme outperforms the conventional scheme in terms of the attainable sum rate and fairness.
the proposed grouping algorithms outperform the state-of-the-art algorithms by up to 2.5 bits/s/Hz in terms of the attainable capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed grouping algorithms outperform the conventional grouping algorithms, in terms of capacity and complexity, for a wide range of network parameters, including the number of users, relays, and antennas.

the proposed transmission protocol can be implemented in a distributed fashion, which makes it particularly suitable for cellular networks with a high degree of mobility and/or for networks with a large number of nodes, such as ad-hoc networks.
, by using the proposed grouping algorithms, the network's capacity can be improved by up to 30% compared to the case of using a single-relay.
